title: Namal remanded over alleged Rs. 100 m  Airbus-linked bribe | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:36
-     - 5

Namal Rajapaksa remanded -Pix by Isuru Perera

Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa was yesterday arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over allegations that he received 

Rs. 100 million in bribes linked to an aircraft procurement deal involving SriLankan Airlines.

Rajapaksa was subsequently produced before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court, which denied bail and ordered that he be remanded until 18 September.

In a statement CIABOC said Rajapaksa was arrested by its investigating officers at around 2:09 p.m. yesterday following more than five hours of questioning.

He had appeared before the Commission at 9:00 a.m. after being instructed to provide a statement as part of the ongoing investigation.

According to CIABOC, the investigation concerns funds allegedly paid as bribes in connection with the purchase of aircraft for SriLankan Airlines.

The Commission alleged that over 

€ 1.4 million had been received as a bribe into an account maintained at Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore under the name BIZ Solutions Inc.

Of this amount, $ 800,000 was allegedly transferred to an OCBC Bank account in Singapore held under Sabre Vision Holdings Ltd., a company owned by a Sri Lankan businessman.

CIABOC alleged that, corresponding to these funds, Rajapaksa received a total of Rs. 100 million from a Sri Lankan businessman on several occasions during 2014 and 2015.

The Commission said the arrest followed an investigation based on a statement obtained from the Sri Lankan businessman, statements provided to CIABOC by officials of France-based Airbus, and documents and other information gathered during the probe.

The latest arrest marks the fourth time Rajapaksa has been taken into custody, following arrests in July 2016 over the Rs.70 million Krrish case, in August 2016 over the HelloCorp/Gowers Corporation money laundering case in which he was acquitted in 2023, and in October 2017 over the Hambantota protest case, while the Krrish and Hambantota cases remain pending.

title: EDB and IESL strengthen capacity of future marine and offshore engineering professionals | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 7

Recognising the strategic importance of the Marine and Offshore sector to Sri Lanka’s export development, the National Export Development Plan (NEDP) 2026–2030 has identified marine-based industries, including boat and shipbuilding, as one of the country’s priority export sectors. 

In line with this national priority, the Export Development Board (EDB), in collaboration with the Institution of Engineers, Sri Lanka (IESL), conducted a one-day capacity-building workshop on Marine and Offshore Engineering (M&OE) for engineering undergraduates, with the aim of strengthening the skills, industry exposure and readiness of Sri Lanka’s future engineering workforce

The workshop was held on 24 August at the University of Moratuwa and was organised through the Marine and Offshore Services (M&OS) Sub-committee on Skills Development under the Advisory Committee on the M&OS Sector, in collaboration with the University of Moratuwa.

The program brought together engineering undergraduates representing the University of Moratuwa, University of Ruhuna, University of Sri Jayewardenepura, General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU), and Ocean University of Sri Lanka. This broad participation provided students from different academic institutions with an opportunity to gain exposure to the Marine and Offshore Services sector and its emerging career and industry opportunities.

Addressing the gathering EDB Director General Erandika Dissanayake said that it is the time to explore the opportunities in mining, oil and gas, nautical tourism, ship building and other related areas.

This initiative will forms part of SLEDB’s broader capacity-building efforts to develop the skills base required to strengthen Sri Lanka’s potential in the marine and offshore services sector.

The workshop featured sessions delivered by academics and industry professionals covering key areas including the marine and offshore industry and its opportunities, welding technology and future trends, upstream petroleum processing and exploration operations, offshore hazard management, Hazard and Operability Studies (HAZOP), offshore pollution management and marine pollution in Sri Lanka.

The program also provided opportunities for participants to engage with experienced professionals through discussion and question-and-answer sessions, enabling students to gain insights into industry requirements and emerging developments beyond their academic curriculum.

The capacity-building initiative is expected to contribute towards increasing awareness among engineering undergraduates of career and professional opportunities within the Marine and Offshore Services sector, while strengthening linkages between academia, professional institutions and industry.

SLEDB, together with its sector stakeholders, intends to continue supporting initiatives that enhance the knowledge, skills and industry exposure of young engineering professionals, contributing to the development of a stronger and more competitive Marine and Offshore Services sector in Sri Lanka. Further it was highlighted that SLEDB with the stakeholders have initiated discussions on developing a Marine and Offshore Blueprint.

NSB joins EDEX Expo Mid-Year 2026 as Official Banking Partner | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 7

National Savings Bank (NSB) has joined hands with EDEX Expo Mid-Year 2026 as its Official Banking Partner for the first time, reaffirming its commitment to empowering Sri Lanka’s youth through education, financial inclusion and access to future opportunities. 

The official launch of EDEX Expo Mid-Year 2026 was held recently, with the participation of NSB Acting General Manager/CO Rohana Bandara Weerakoon in the launching ceremony, representing the bank. 

Sri Lanka’s largest and longest-running education and job exhibition, EDEX Expo Mid-Year 2026 will be held on 5 and 6 September 2026 at the BMICH, Colombo. Organised continuously since 2004 by the Royal College Union, EDEX brings together local and international higher education institutions, professional and vocational education providers, employers, Government institutions and other public and private sector organisations. 

The partnership reflects NSB’s commitment to supporting young Sri Lankans as they navigate an increasingly competitive and rapidly changing education and employment landscape. Recognising the importance of financial empowerment alongside education, NSB offers solutions to support students, parents and young professionals in achieving their aspirations. 

These include the NSB I’M account for youth aged 19 to 35 years and NSB Buddhi, an education loan facility supporting local and overseas degree programs. The bank also provides personal loan facilities, balance confirmation services for visa applications, foreign currency services and Telegraphic Transfer (TT) facilities, subject to applicable terms and conditions. NSB’s digital banking ecosystem, including the NSB Pay App, Digital Banking and QR payment facilities, further enables customers to manage their finances conveniently. 

Weerakoon said: “At NSB, we believe that education and financial empowerment must go hand in hand. Supporting young people in achieving their aspirations is an investment in the future of our nation. We are proud to partner with EDEX and look forward to making a meaningful contribution to this important national initiative.” NSB will be present at the EDEX Expo, providing students, parents and young professionals with an opportunity to engage with the Bank and explore financial solutions supporting their education and future.

title: SLC hosts Mass Communication students of University of Kelaniya | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 1

Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) hosted 160 students from the Mass Communication Department of the University of Kelaniya as part of an educational field visit aimed at providing them with practical exposure to sports journalism and media operations of an international sport event.

As part of the visit, the students, accompanied by their academic staff, visited the RPICS, Colombo, where they were given the opportunity to conduct a field study on sports journalism, with a particular focus on cricket reporting, sports photography and managing international media operations.

The field study was conducted during the Sri Lanka vs. India Under-19 second four-day game, providing the students with valuable hands-on experience in Press Box operations, live sports reporting and sports photography.

The Sri Lanka Cricket Media Unit also conducted a presentation on “Professional Practices in Sports Journalism”, followed by a productive Q&A session. The students had the opportunity to engage with industry professionals, including professional photographers covering international cricket, and gain insights into the practical aspects and challenges of working in sports media.

The visit provided an excellent opportunity for the students to bridge classroom learning with real-world media practice, while gaining a better understanding of the professional standards and responsibilities involved in sports journalism.

The academic staff who accompanied the students included Senior Lecturer Saman Rajapaksha; Ms. Amali Nandasiri and Mrs. Dilini Gamage, Probationary Lecturer Mrs. Amani Rupasingha; and Assistant Lecturers Ms. Nipuni Bhagya and Savindu Iroshan.

The initiative is part of Sri Lanka Cricket’s commitment to its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program, aimed at empowering and nurturing the next generation of professionals and contributing to the future development of the nation.

title: Kusal Mendis ruled out of England T20I series, Asalanka to captain | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 3

Charith Asalanka returns to Sri Lanka T20I captaincy for the England tour

Dasun Shanaka celebrating the fastest hundred off 39 balls in CPL history

Pavan Rathnayake and Dilshan Madushanka the two replacements

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

Kusal Mendis who was named captain for the two white ball series in England has been ruled out of the three-match T20I series along with left-arm fast bowler Binura Fernando.

Both players are recovering from injuries and have yet to prove their fitness by playing in a match.

Charith Asalanka who was named vice-captain for the T20I and ODI series will lead Sri Lanka in the three T20I matches against England commencing 15 September at Southampton. The second and third matches will take place at Cardiff (17 September) and Manchester (19 September).

Asalanka returns to the T20I captaincy after being ditched from the job for a combination of poor form and his hesitance to play on during Sri Lanka’s tour of Pakistan last year citing security concerns.

Mendis and Fernando have been replaced in the 16-member squad by Pavan Rathnayake and Dilshan Madushanka. Both these players were named in Sri Lanka’s ODI squad to England, but will now have the opportunity to play in both formats.

By naming Mendis captain for England as it was pointed out in these columns, the selectors were taking a gamble as he had not conformed to their policy of playing in a match before being considered for selection coming back from an injury.

Saner counsel seems to have prevailed and Mendis has been quite rightly been kept behind to prove his fitness at least before the three-match ODI series which commences on 22 September.

Mendis suffered a right hamstring injury during the Lanka Premier League (LPL) and has been undergoing rehabilitation at the High Performance Centre (HPC). He is expected to play for SSC in the Major Club 50-over and T20 tournaments next week.

Fernando, who sustained a back injury during the LPL, has also been undergoing rehabilitation at the HPC and has not played a match yet. As he is part of only the T20I squad he will miss the tour to England.

Sri Lanka’s T20I squad will leave for England today with the ODI squad due to follow on 18 September.

Asalanka, Dasun Shanaka, Wanindu Hasaranga and Maheesh Theekshana are due to join the T20I squad in England from the Caribbean where they are currently taking part in the Caribbean Premier League (CPL).

Shanaka set ablaze the CPL on Thursday, by slamming the fastest century in the tournament’s history – off 39 balls for St Kitts and Nevis Patriots who defeated St Lucia’s Kings by a whopping 137 runs – the biggest margin of victory in the CPL. Shanaka’s strike rate of 281.39 was also the highest for a century in the CPL. In his innings of 121* off 43 balls Shanaka slammed 8 fours and 12 sixes, with 4 sixes and a four coming off the final over of the innings. Amongst the bowlers who took a beating from Shanaka’s broad bat were Sri Lankan team mate Maheesh Theekshana who went for 48 runs, Matthew Forde, Joshua Bishop, Keon Gaston and Roston Chase.

T20I Squad (revised): Pathum Nissanka, Kamil Mishara, Lahiru Udara, Kamindu Mendis, Charith Asalanka (Captain), Pavan Rathnayake, Janith Liyanage, Dasun Shanaka, Dunith Wellalage, Wanindu Hasaranga, Maheesh Theekshana, Tharindu Rathnayake, Dushmantha Chameera, Eshan Malinga, Nuwan Thushara, Dilshan Madushanka.

title: Dasun Shanaka smashes fastest CPL century | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 3

St. Kitts and Nevis Patriots registered a thumping 137-run win over the Saint Lucia Kings at Basseterre on Thursday (September 3). Piling on 235 for 4 on the back of Dasun Shanaka’s record century, the Patriots rolled their opponents out for just 98 with Jeremiah Louis picking up five wickets.

Asked to bat first, the Patriots began modestly, scoring just 10 runs from the first three overs while also losing Kyle Mayers. The tempo shifted in the third over with Matthew Forde conceding a six, four and five wides. Andre Fletcher then smashed Maheesh Theekshana for 19 runs in the following over before three more boundaries came in the sixth, taking the Patriots to 59 for 1 at the end of the Powerplay.

Fletcher was dropped in the seventh over and promptly brought up fifty, off just 23 balls, in the seventh over. Roston Chase broke the 81-run stand between Fletcher and Johnson Charles by dismissing the latter in the 10th over but the real carnage was yet to unfold. Shanaka began his brutal assault by smashing Joshua Bishop for two fours and followed it up with two sixes against Chase.

The Kings dismissed Fletcher and Jason Holder in the space of two overs but there was no respite with Shanaka firing on all cylinders. He brought up fifty off just 24 balls before reaching his century off just 39 deliveries - the fastest in the CPL. He struck four sixes and a boundary off the final over as the Patriots finished with an imposing 235 for 4.

The Kings’ chase never really got off the ground. After losing Kamil Pooran in the very first over, they also lost John Campbell and Charith Asalanka inside the Powerplay to end up with just 46 for 3 from the phase. Wanindu Hasaranga dismissed Obus Pienaar in the following over and then it was the Jeremiah Louis show. Brought into the attack in the 10th over, Louis struck straightaway, removing Chase and Forde off successive deliveries. Tim Seifert, who had been fighting a lone battle, was then sent back by Ashmead Nedd in the following over.

Louis returned to claim Joshua Bishop before wrapping the innings up by dismissing Theekshana and Amari Goodridge in the 14th over. The Kings were skittled out for just 98 with only three batters getting into double figures.

Scores: 

St Kitts and Nevis Patriots 235/4 in 20 overs (Dasun Shanaka 121*, Andre Fletcher 64; Matthew Forde 2-48) beat Saint Lucia Kings 98 all-out in 13.5 overs (Tim Seifert 50; Jeremiah Louis 5-10)

title: Sri Lanka’s young sevens teams ready for Asia Under-18 Championship in China | Daily FT
summary:

Sri Lanka’s boys’ and girls’ rugby sevens teams are set to compete in the Asia Rugby Under-18 Sevens Championship, which will be played in China today and tomorrow, with the country’s rising stars aiming to make their mark against the continent’s best young talent.

The boys’ tournament features nine teams divided into two groups. Sri Lanka has been drawn in a challenging Group A alongside Hong Kong China, Malaysia and India, while Group B consists of hosts China, Chinese Taipei, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and the UAE.

The Sri Lankan boys’ outfit will be captained by Mohamed Fawaz and coached by Rajeew Perera, with Bhanuka Nanayakkara serving as assistant coach and Imran Thalagampe as team manager.

The side will be looking to produce strong performances against experienced regional rivals and challenge for a place in the knockout stages.

The girls’ competition will feature eight teams split into two groups. Sri Lanka is placed in Group C with China, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, while Group D includes Hong Kong China, India, Malaysia and the UAE.

Ayusha Jeewamani will lead the Sri Lankan girls’ team under the guidance of head coach Shamly Nawas, assisted by Asela Deshapriya, with Thilini Senanayake serving as team manager. (SJ)

title: Abans crowned MCA ‘C’ Division Champions | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 3

Elevated to ‘B’ Division

Abans, in Partnership with LG emerged champions of the Mercantile Cricket Association (MCA) ‘C’ Division Cricket Tournament, defeating Sampath Bank in the final played at the CCC Grounds on August 21, 2026. Subsequently, the Abans team was also elevated to ‘B’ Division with this win. The team came through with a commanding performance to post 284 all out, before dismissing Sampath Bank for 151, securing the championship with a comprehensive 133-run victory.

Led by Sudara Dakshina, the Abans team displayed an impressive all-round performance, with their batting laying the foundation for a convincing win. Shahan Kaushalya top-scored with an outstanding 80 runs off 63 balls, including nine fours and two sixes. He was well supported by Duranka Silva, who struck a fluent 76 off 60 balls, with six fours and seven sixes, while Tharusha Fernando contributed a valuable 63 off 71 balls, including nine fours and two sixes.

With the ball, Kaveesha Dulanjana delivered a winning spell, claiming an exceptional 6 wickets for 33 runs in 6.4 overs. His outstanding performance earned him both the Best Bowler of the Final award and the prestigious Man of the Final title.

The individual awards reflected Abans’ dominance, with Shahan Kaushalya named Best Batsman of the Final, while Kaveesha Dulanjana was recognised for his decisive contribution with the ball with the award for Best Bowler of the Final, as well as Man of the Final.

The MCA, Sri Lanka’s premier organisation dedicated to promoting cricket among the mercantile community, continues to provide a competitive platform for corporate teams and players to showcase their talent. Abans’ triumph adds another memorable chapter to the 2026 MCA Division Cricket Tournament.

title: Sri Lanka Rugby appoints Marija as Head Coach | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 5 September 2026 00:00
-     - 2

Fazil Marija

By Shamseer Jaleel

Sri Lanka Rugby (SLR) has appointed former national captain, Kandy SC and Trinity College Coach Fazil Marija as its Head Coach of the Sri Lanka Men’s Sevens team, replacing Peter Woods and his team, following a review of the team’s performance at the opening leg of the Asia Rugby Sevens in China.

The decision comes after Sri Lanka finished seventh in the opening leg, a result that fell below the expectations of SLR as the team continues its preparations for the Asian Games.

Marija will be supported by Nigel Ratwatte as Assistant Coach and Tharaka Alagama as Strength and Conditioning Coach, with the new coaching team taking charge with immediate effect for the Asian Games in Japan as well as the Asia Rugby second leg in Colombo.

The new coaching staff will commence their first session on 7 September.
